page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, storage-optimized instance powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at 3.2 GHz, it features 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs with 320 MB of L3 cache, supporting instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The server is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage capacity is led by 60,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, supplemented by a 100 Gbps baseline network connection.

In benchmark evaluations, the i7ie.metal-24xl demonstrates top-tier multi-core compute and memory capabilities. Multi-core performance tests such as stress-ng and PassMark CPU show high execution scores, while software compilation and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression register in the top 10% of tested instances. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 289.33 GB/sec. Database operations and static web serving throughput exhibit top-tier throughput at 133.13 GB/sec, while CPU-based LLM prompt processing for medium and large models performs strongly.

The server offers exceptional resource density by pairing 60,000 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage with 768 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory on a single bare-metal host. This minimizes external network storage dependencies and virtualization overhead. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of discrete GPU hardware, shifting parallel matrix workloads entirely onto CPU extensions like AMX, alongside the requirement to manage high-capacity local ephemeral storage.

The instance is suited for large-scale enterprise databases, data warehousing, high-throughput analytics, software compilation, and memory-intensive ETL pipelines that require massive local disk space and sustained parallel compute capabilities.
